name: 1920s candlestick phone
about: A narrow, frying carbon-mic voice on a long crackly line from the 1920s.

name: Long distance call, 1930s
about: A faint voice from across the country, thin and hissing, with its own echo trailing behind.

name: Party line with the neighbors
about: An old shared country line: clicks as neighbors pick up and their chatter murmuring under you.

name: 1950s rotary desk phone
about: The classic landline sound: a warm, boxy voice squeezed into the old telephone band.

name: Kitchen wall phone, long cord
about: Someone calling from a tiled kitchen, the room ringing around them on an old wall phone.

name: 1980s cordless phone
about: An early cordless handset: hiss that breathes with each word and a swish now and then.

name: Cordless phone, out of range
about: Walked too far from the base: the voice sinks into rushing static and swishing dropouts.

name: 1980s car phone
about: A big analog car phone with the engine rumbling under every word and a hissing radio link.

name: 1990s cell phone
about: An early digital mobile: coarse coded speech, a buzz from the radio and a gargle on weak moments.

name: 2000s flip phone
about: A pocket flip phone: swirly coding, warbling noise cleanup and a level that pumps.

name: Phone tucked under the chin
about: A cell phone squashed between shoulder and cheek, the mic half covered and muffled.

name: Cheap hotel room phone
about: The bedside phone of a tired motel: boxy, buzzing and full of hiss.

name: Bad cell signal
about: One bar of signal: the voice gargles, breaks into burbles and drops whole syllables.

name: Call dropping out
about: A flip phone call that keeps cutting to silence mid-word, then coming back.

name: Calling from the basement
about: Down in a concrete stairwell with almost no signal, the echo and the gargle fighting.

name: Robot glitches on a weak call
about: An internet call where every lost moment turns into a buzzing metallic robot.

name: Stuttering frozen call
about: The line freezes and repeats the same scrap of sound before jumping ahead.

name: Calling from a tunnel
about: Driving into a long tunnel: the voice gets boomy and hollow as the signal fades.

name: Hands-free in a moving car
about: A driver on speaker in the car, the engine droning and the phone's level pumping.

name: Calling from a windy hill
about: Wind blasting the phone's mic while someone shouts from an exposed hilltop.

name: Crossed lines
about: Another conversation has leaked onto your line and mumbles away under the voice.

name: Internet call
about: A typical computer call: clear enough, with noise cleanup and a hiccup now and then.

name: Video call, frozen picture
about: A starving video call: swirly, watery voice that freezes and repeats when the picture stalls.

name: Laptop meeting, far from the mic
about: Someone leaning back from their laptop in an office, roomy and thin through little speakers.

name: Cheap earbud mic
about: Talking through the little mic on a cheap earbud cable: thin, scratchy and squeezed.

name: Wireless headset breaking up
about: A wireless headset at the edge of its range: underwater swirl and tiny gaps.

name: Satellite phone with a delay
about: A rebuilt robotic voice bounced off a satellite, with your words echoing back late.

name: Secure scrambled phone
about: A coded military phone line: the voice rebuilt from a few numbers, buzzy and inhuman.

name: Dialed into an online meeting
about: Someone joining a computer meeting from a cell phone: coded twice and twice as squeezed.

name: Desk speakerphone
about: A desk speakerphone: boxy, a little roomy, and it clips the start of every sentence.

name: Speakerphone across a big room
about: Talking to the conference phone from the far end of a long, echoing meeting room.

name: Conference call from a busy office
about: A speakerphone in an open office, colleagues chattering behind the person talking.

name: Conference call with echo
about: A meeting line where your own words leak back a moment later from the far speaker.

name: Phone face up on the table
about: A call on loudspeaker from a phone lying on the kitchen table, tinny and rattling.

name: Call through the car stereo
about: A phone call played through the car speakers while you cruise down the highway.

name: Speakerphone in a crowded van
about: Everyone leaning toward one phone in a rattling van, the voice tinny over the crowd.

name: Payphone in the rain
about: A crackly street payphone pressed to your ear while rain pours on the pavement around you.

name: Caller at a payphone, storm
about: Someone calling from a booth with rain hammering on it, the downpour coming down the line.

name: Airport payphone
about: A payphone in a busy terminal, suitcases rolling and announcements echoing behind you.

name: Payphone on the subway platform
about: A grimy underground payphone while trains rumble in and squeal along the platform.

name: Phone booth on a city corner
about: A caller shut in a glass booth, the little box ringing around them, traffic outside.

name: Collect call from a truck stop
about: A late-night payphone call with idling rigs rumbling and a mains hum on the line.

name: Payphone in the laundromat
about: Calling home from the wall phone while dryers tumble and a washer thumps through its spin.

name: Answering machine message
about: The beep, then your message on a tiny wobbly tape with hiss and a whining motor.

name: Worn answering machine tape
about: An old message tape recorded over a hundred times, wobbling and buried in hiss.

name: Digital voicemail
about: A cell message stored in a few coarse bits, grainy hiss riding every word.

name: Automated phone menu
about: A flat, over-polished recorded menu voice asking you to press one.

name: Message played back too fast
about: The answering machine's motor races, so the message squeaks by at double speed.

name: Machine with a dragging tape
about: A tired machine whose tape drags, so the caller comes out slow, low and seasick.

name: Family walkie-talkie
about: A handheld radio: a click as you key up, faint hiss, and a burst of squelch when you let go.

name: Toy walkie-talkie
about: A plastic toy radio from a birthday party: thin, hissy and crunchy.

name: Soldier's field radio
about: A rugged field radio, heavily squeezed and rough, with a low tone when the talker lets go.

name: Night guard in the parking garage
about: A security guard radioing in from an echoing concrete garage, a chirp after each call.

name: Ski patrol in a blizzard
about: A rescue radio crackling through a howling snowstorm on the mountain.

name: Construction crew radio
about: A foreman shouting into a clipped radio over jackhammers and a reversing digger.

name: Walkie-talkie at summer camp
about: A crackly radio from the next cabin over, crickets singing in the warm dark.

name: Fishing boat radio
about: Another boat calling on the marine handset while your engine chugs and waves slap the hull.

name: CB trucker
about: A trucker on the citizens band: crackling static, a whistle on the channel and a hot mic.

name: CB with an echo mic
about: A driver with an echo box wired into the mic, every word repeating, then a sign-off tone.

name: Far-off CB skip
about: A voice from a thousand miles away, fading in and out under static and whistles.

name: Overmodulated CB, big amplifier
about: A rig pushed way too hard: the voice splatters and crunches, then a sign-off beep.

name: CB in the truck cab
about: The CB speaker crackling in the cab while the truck roars down the highway.

name: Deep-voiced night driver
about: A low, gravelly long-haul voice on the CB with a touch of echo in the mic.

name: Police scanner
about: Dispatch chatter on a desktop scanner: squeezed and harsh with a squelch tail on every call.

name: Digital police radio
about: The watery robotic warble of a modern digital dispatch channel.

name: Air traffic control tower
about: A crisp, squeezed controller on the aviation band, with a carrier thump on each call.

name: Pilot calling the tower
about: A pilot on the radio from a small plane, the engine droning through the headset mic.

name: Taxi dispatch radio
about: The cab's dash radio squawking out the next fare over the noise of the city.

name: Scanner hopping channels
about: A scanner jumping from channel to channel, catching scraps of speech between squelch bursts.

name: Digital radio breaking up
about: A digital channel at the edge of range, the voice dissolving into bubbling robot errors.

name: Ambulance crew radio
about: A paramedic calling in on a digital handset while a siren wails across the city.

name: Ham radio on sideband
about: A ham operator across the world: narrow sideband voice, deep fades and crackling air.

name: Mistuned sideband squawk
about: A sideband signal tuned too high, so the voice squawks like a sing-song duck.

name: Sideband tuned too low
about: The receiver sits below the signal and the voice turns into a growling, muddy mumble.

name: Numbers station at midnight
about: A flat, emotionless voice reading on shortwave, with a radar knocking in the static.

name: Shortwave news from overseas
about: An international news broadcast swimming in and out, teletype tones chattering beside it.

name: Ship-to-shore radio
about: A captain calling the harbor on a crackling marine set, gulls and a foghorn by the docks.

name: Polar research station radio
about: A lonely voice from a station at the bottom of the world, a storm battering the hut.

name: Kitchen table AM radio
about: A little table radio tuned to an AM talk station: dense, warm and a bit of static.

name: Pocket transistor radio
about: A tiny 1960s transistor radio held to your ear, tinny and bright.

name: Car radio on the AM dial
about: An AM station on the dashboard radio, alternator whine and all, rolling down the road.

name: Lost between stations
about: The dial between two stations: a faint voice drowning in static, whistles and another show.

name: Far-off station at night
about: A distant city's station skipping in after dark, swelling and fading with a whistle.

name: Talk radio caller on air
about: A listener phoning in to a talk show, their cell call squashed again by the station.

name: Weather band robot voice
about: The flat machine voice of a weather radio reading the forecast through a little speaker.

name: Pirate radio from a basement
about: An unlicensed station run from a cramped room: crunchy, crushed and barely holding on.

name: Oldies station on AM
about: A golden-age disc jockey on the AM dial, the studio echo ringing behind every word.

name: FM fading in the car
about: An FM station at the edge of town: hiss rising and the voice fluttering as the car drives on.

name: Emergency broadcast in a storm
about: An urgent bulletin crackling from the kitchen radio while thunder rolls outside the window.

name: Spinning the radio dial
about: Turning the knob past station after station, your voice flickering in and out of the static.

name: Radio just off the station
about: The dial a hair off the station: the voice turns thin, edgy and buzzing.

name: Mission control
about: Ground control talking to a spacecraft in orbit, a beep tone before and after each call.

name: Calling from the moon
about: A voice from the lunar surface, narrow and hissing, the far echo coming back seconds later.

name: Signal from a deep space probe
about: A thin, fragile voice from the far edge of the solar system, breaking up in the hiss.

name: Astronaut in a helmet
about: Talking inside a closed space helmet, the visor ringing close around your mouth.

name: Launch pad countdown
about: The launch director on the loop while a rocket thunders off the pad in the distance.

name: Video call from orbit
about: An astronaut calling home from the space station, the picture link swirling and catching.

name: Drive-through speaker
about: The crushed, crackling order box at a fast food window.

name: Apartment door buzzer
about: A visitor speaking from the metal box by the front door, buzzing and ringing.

name: Classroom wall speaker
about: The morning announcements from the box above the blackboard, echoing round the room.

name: Baby monitor
about: An old nursery monitor: hiss that breathes with every word and the soft room around you.

name: Baby monitor hearing the neighbors
about: The monitor picks up a neighbor's cordless phone, garbled chatter crackling over you.

name: Elevator emergency phone
about: Someone stuck in a lift, talking through the buzzing speaker grille in the steel box.

name: Doorbell camera on the porch
about: A voice from the tiny speaker of a video doorbell, swirly and tinny, leaves rustling outside.

name: Ship's engine room phone
about: A sailor shouting up to the bridge from below decks, the diesels roaring down the tinny line.

name: Tin-can phone
about: Two soup cans and a taut string: thin, metallic and ringing, with a zing down the line.

name: Coffee cans on a long string
about: Big coffee cans stretched across the yard, deeper and boomy, the string springing.

name: Paper cup phone
about: Two paper cups and a string: soft, papery and close.

name: Talking down a garden hose
about: Shouting into one end of a long hose: hollow, tubey and ringing.

name: Plastic toy telephone
about: A child's toy phone with a little speaker that rattles and crackles on loud words.
